title: How to clean messy Excel data in 10 minutes with pandas
text: Every messy Excel file has the same five problems. Here is the exact sequence I run, in order, every single time. Thanks for reading Learn with Jashwanth! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work. STEP 1: INSPECT (2 MINUTES) df = pd.read_excel('messy.xlsx') print(df.shape) print(df.dtypes) print(df.isnull().sum()) You cannot fix what you have not measured. This tells you the damage in thirty seconds. STEP 2: FIX HEADERS AND TYPES (3 MINUTES) df.columns = df.columns.str.strip().str.lower().str.replace(' ', '_') df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'], errors='coerce') df['amount'] = pd.to_numeric(df['amount'], errors='coerce') Dirty column names and wrong types cause 80% of downstream errors. Fix them before anything else. STEP 3: HANDLE MISSING VALUES (3 MINUTES) df = df.dropna(subset=['customer_id']) # rows useless without an ID df['region'] = df['region'].fillna('Unknown') # categories get a label df['amount'] = df['amount'].fillna(df['amount'].median()) # numbers get the median Three different missing-value strategies for three different column types. That distinction is the whole game. STEP 4: KILL DUPLICATES (2 MINUTES) df = df.drop_duplicates() print(df.shape) # confirm how many rows died Done. Ten minutes, and the file is analysis-ready. Here's my ask: reply with the messiest Excel horror story you have survived. I read every reply, and the worst one gets featured next week. Stop fearing messy files. They are all the same five problems. 🚀 What is your step one when a dirty file lands? Comment below. — Jashwanth Dasari Thanks for reading Learn with Jashwanth! title: Your first data job doesn't need machine learning
text: I spent three months learning neural networks before I could write a proper JOIN. That was backwards, and it cost me interviews. THE CLAIM Most beginners study machine learning before they can query a database. I did the same. Here is my claim: SQL will get you hired, machine learning will get you promoted, and the order matters more than either skill alone. WHY EVERYONE DISAGREES Because ML looks like the future and SQL looks like plumbing. Courses sell "AI" and "deep learning" because those words sell. Nobody markets a course called "42 boring JOINs that change your career." But the job market does not care about course marketing. It cares about what you can do on day one. WHAT DATA JOBS ACTUALLY ASK FOR Strip the buzzwords from entry level data postings and the same pattern repeats: 📊 Pull data from three tables and join them without duplicating rows 📊 Answer "what changed last month" with a GROUP BY, not a model 📊 Clean messy timestamps, nulls, and duplicate keys inside the query itself 📊 Build one dashboard metric a stakeholder actually trusts 📊 Explain the result in one sentence a non-technical manager understands Every one of those is SQL plus judgment. None of them need gradient descent. Here is the kind of query that impresses hiring managers more than a Kaggle notebook: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', signup_date) AS cohort, COUNT(*) AS users, SUM(CASE WHEN last_active >= CURRENT_DATE - 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_30d, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN last_active >= CURRENT_DATE - 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS retention_pct FROM users GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1; Thanks for reading Learn with Jashwanth! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work. Twelve lines. It answers a question a CEO would actually ask. Most "ML-ready" beginners I meet cannot write it, because tutorials never made them. WHEN ML ACTUALLY MATTERS I am not saying skip machine learning forever. Learn it after SQL, after pandas, after one real project with messy data. ML is the second floor. SQL is the foundation. You cannot frame a prediction problem if you cannot first describe the data with a query. The analysts who learn ML first build models on data they cannot explain. The ones who learn SQL first build models on data they understand. Here's my ask: reply and tell me where you stand in the SQL vs ML order right now. Stuck on window functions? Halfway through a deep learning course? I read every reply, and I will tell you exactly what I would learn next. Master the boring skill first. The exciting ones get easier after. 🚀 What is the one SQL concept that finally clicked for you, and what made it click? Tell me in the comments. — Jashwanth Dasari

title: I finally started the newsletter I kept putting off
text: Hey, Jashwanth here. For months I've been sharing data tips, AI workflows, and career resources with 10,000+ of you on LinkedIn. And every week someone asks me: "where can I learn all of this properly, in one place?" So here it is: Learn with Jashwanth , my new home for everything I learn, build, and break in data science and AI. WHAT YOU'LL GET HERE Every day, one short and practical post. No fluff, no 40-minute reads. Things like: 📊 Pandas and SQL tricks that save you hours every single week 🤖 AI workflows I actually use: Copilot, agents, automation 🧠 ML concepts explained the way I wish someone had explained them to me 💼 Career resources: roadmaps, GitHub repos, interview prep that actually works WHY I'M DOING THIS I learn best by teaching. Everything I post here is something I've used in real work: at StyleCraft, in my FAU research, or in the GDG community I run. If it didn't survive contact with a real dataset, it doesn't make the cut. WHO THIS IS FOR Students and early-career folks in data and AI who want practical skills, not textbook theory. If that's you, you're in the right place. Here's my ask: hit subscribe (it's free, and staying that way), and reply to this email with ONE topic you want me to break down. I read every reply, and your suggestions will literally shape what I write next. Let's learn together. Day 1 starts now. 🚀 What's the one data or AI skill you want to master before this year ends? Drop it in the comments. —Jashwanth Dasari
